sources.actual_observation: The thesis describes low-gradient, sheet-like runoff and dispersed temporary or permanent lagoons. Its Figure50 distinguishes western R1 and eastern R2, labels Chadilauquen and regional hydrological systems, and locates surrounding towns. It does not depict a continuous selected river.
sources.map_attribution: Printed p.92 explicitly describes preparation of Figure50 for the thesis study area. Figures48–49 are separately credited as adaptations of UNLPam2015; those figures were not used as inspected map evidence and the underlying inventory was not separately acquired.
sources.limits: The frame covers the selected extent, but a label masks part of the northern interval. Scale and thematic purpose do not resolve selected channel, lagoon or terminal links. Regional groundwater direction is not surface-channel evidence. No present hydrological state is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening through Doutor Loretti to Alto Imbé
correspondence.finding: The municipal original shows the selected opening corridor southwest of Doutor Loretti, its northeastward continuation through the settlement and the joining reach at Alto Imbé. The basin study independently describes the upper Imbé valley through the Trajano de Morais and Dr. Loretti setting. The study also discusses a reservoir at Nova Esperança upstream in Trajano de Morais; it is not inserted into this selection merely because it belongs to the same basin.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Imbé continuation and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: The municipal map traces the valley northeast past the Imbé/Macuco do Imbé setting to the Água Limpa and Santo Antônio do Imbé joining area and the repeatedly labelled Rio do Imbé corridor. The state map independently locates that named river in the same valley. Names of tributaries and settlements are kept distinct.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern middle-valley side passage
correspondence.finding: The selection turns into the northern parallel-drainage setting below Sossego and toward the Rio do Norte junction. The detailed municipal map shows the labelled Rio do Imbé farther south and other northern channels; the state map generalizes them. A continuous source correspondence for the selected transfer between these parallel passages is not established. Shared valley position and the Imbé name alone do not close this link.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Imbé alluvial and flood-prone approach to Lagoa de Cima
correspondence.finding: The state original depicts the lower Imbé/Mocotó joining setting, a flood-prone corridor and an inlet on the southwest side of Lagoa de Cima. The independent basin study identifies the Imbé alluvial lowland and its lagoon-side outlet, with historical artificial drainage in the valley. These establish the regional approach and wetland setting, but do not independently supply each local channel connection absent from the detailed municipal coverage.

correspondence.component_scope: Lagoa de Cima passage and east outlet
correspondence.finding: The named lake and its southwest river entry are visible on the state original. Its east/northeast outlet is represented only by a short channel and nearby separate watercourses; the acquired map does not trace the complete selected east-going continuation. The basin study ends at the lagoon-side basin setting and cannot fill the downstream connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Intervening lowland river, urban approach and southward connection
correspondence.finding: The state original shows a drainage network southwest of Campos dos Goytacazes and north of Lagoa Feia, but does not continuously connect the selected route back to the Lagoa de Cima outlet. The successful Quissamã map begins farther south. No unseen Campos municipal map or stopped article is used to bridge this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Lagoa Feia inflow and northeastern lake-margin passage
correspondence.finding: Quissamã depicts a northern inflow labelled Rio do Imbé, the Rio Macaco and Canal do Nicolau joins, Lagoa Feia, its northern/eastern lobes, and the Lagoa da Jararaca connection. The selected route follows the northeastern margin and lobe setting rather than simply crossing the central lake. The originals identify these receiving-water settings but do not establish every selected lobe-to-lobe or intervening margin through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern lowland drainage and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: Quissamã shows the eastern Lagoa Feia exit, channels near the locality Canal das Flechas, the Pernambuco drainage and the continuation toward Barra Furado. The selected approach runs farther north/east across this drainage mosaic before reaching the coastal end. The inspected originals do not establish a continuous passage for that selected approach; the mapped central lake outlet is not substituted for it. Absence of an operation label is not the issue.

correspondence.component_scope: Atlantic terminal beside Barra do Furado
correspondence.finding: The originals identify the Atlantic receiving coast and show a channel opening in the Barra Furado/Quissamã boundary setting. This supports the regional receiving-water identity and coastal endpoint setting. It does not resolve the unestablished final connection from the selection’s upstream eastern lowland route. No assertion about modern inlet position, gates or current tidal flow is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening before the mapped Jorquencal or Escalera course
correspondence.finding: The selected opening makes a westward and southwestward approach north and east of the first depicted channel junction. The first two stored parts and the approach into the third are not supplied with a corresponding natural-watercourse line. The mapped northern and eastern channel approaches cannot be substituted for this chosen opening. The surface layer supplies no lake or salar footprint here that would explain the missing connection. No natural-source position or absence of an actual watercourse is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern upper corridor and Turipite joining setting
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the connected southwestern drainage explicitly labeled Q. Jorquencal o Escalera. Northern feeders enter separately, and the Q. Turipite approach joins from the north and northwest near the lower part of this interval. Short offsets generalize channel bends, but the selected receiving corridor and these joins are accounted for at ordinary regional scale. The name is not extended over the unsupported northeastern opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Puripica junction and the source-labeled Puritama reach
correspondence.finding: The selected route reaches the separate Q. Puripica approach from the east and continues southwest along the connected channel labeled Río Puritama in the IGM rendering. It does not ascend Puripica. This records the label placement actually shown by the source, without asserting an official name-transition point at either the confluence or a stored-part boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern and southern Vilama receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestern continuation and southward turn correspond to the channel subsequently labeled Río Vilama. The separate Q. de Chaxa drainage lies to the east, while Río San Pedro occupies a distinct western corridor. The lower selected bends locally generalize the Vilama course. This supports a bounded upper Vilama component, not a Vilama name for the long salar-interior selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Landward transfer east of Vilama and approach to the northern salar margin
correspondence.finding: The selection departs eastward from the independently drawn Vilama corridor toward the lower Q. de Chaxa vicinity, then extends south beyond that eastern channel ending to the northern salar margin. Neither a complete connecting natural channel between the two depicted drainages nor the subsequent landward southward through-link is shown. The waterbody rendering begins at the northern salar margin near the beginning of stored part 13 and does not cover the preceding landward interval. The mapped salar therefore explains the downstream surface passage but cannot by itself close this missing approach. No canal, diversion, dry wash continuity or current hydraulic connection is invented.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Salar de Atacama entry and interior southward passage
correspondence.finding: After crossing the mapped northern margin, the selected route remains inside the broad salt-flat footprint and continues south. The surface attributes name this feature Salar de Atacama and classify it as Salar. Natural-watercourse linework depicts separate marginal and interior features but does not draw one river following the complete selected interior. The geography of the salt-flat passage is accounted for; the unresolved landward inlet remains a separate gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle salar crossing and intersection with separately mapped San Pedro drainage
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues south and southwest inside the mapped salar, then turns west across the setting of separate linework including a channel labeled Río San Pedro. It does not follow that named western drainage continuously. The source supplies the salar surface and spatial relationships of the nearby channel network; it does not establish that crossing or approaching the named line makes the complete selected route Río San Pedro, nor that there is one natural channel along each modeled interior segment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern salt-flat passage, final loop and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The remaining selection runs south through the broad mapped salar and makes a compact western and northern loop before ending within its interior. The terminal-only surface attribute response identifies the feature at the actual selected tip as Salar de Atacama, type Salar. Thus the terminal identity is independently supported by the source, rather than inferred from the model endorheic flag. The tip is not established as a named river mouth, a lagoon outlet, the lowest point of the salar or a currently inundated location. No continuous natural-river channel is mapped along the final loop.

correspondence.component_scope: Dry-channel, lake, reservoir and managed-passage scope
correspondence.finding: The inspected natural-watercourse and surface originals distinguish the upper named drainage network from the large Salar de Atacama passage. No selected reservoir or specific named lagoon traversal is established, and no managed transfer is identified. A generic waterbody rendering cannot establish permanent open water, current discharge, every small impoundment, or all engineered works. Its extensive salar footprint geographically accounts for the downstream surface segments, while the northeastern opening and landward river-to-salar transfer remain material gaps.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening and initial northwestward approach
correspondence.finding: The pinned selection begins in inland western Devon and initially trends northwest. No inspected primary cartography identifies the opening or establishes its connection to the subsequent course. The independent field study concerns a different, more easterly site and supplies no opening evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward reach and first intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: The selected upper westward continuation and its stored joins lack an independently inspected hydrographic depiction. Neither the regional coastal description nor the geological-map bibliography proves these through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: Long middle westward to northwestward corridor
correspondence.finding: No readable permitted map was obtained to associate the long middle course and its bends with specific streams, lake passages or terrain corridors. The selected line alone is orientation, not source correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward turn and lower inland continuation
correspondence.finding: The northward turn, intervening joins and lower inland continuation remain without ordinary source correspondence. No claim is made that this selected stretch crosses present glacier ice, follows a relict subglacial channel, or lacks local ponds and wetlands.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northwestward coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The approach toward the western Devon coast has not been connected to a depicted outlet channel. Coastal prose locates the surrounding low deltaic shore, but does not establish these selected lower reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: Final stored part and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: ARC402 describes an extensive delta and drying flats north of Dragleybeck Inlet, followed by Baring Bay with mudflats and lagoons. This is consistent with the broad selected terminal vicinity on Wellington Channel. It does not identify the chosen final outlet or its full inland connection. The selected rendered endpoint differs from the modeled source sea endpoint; neither was substituted for the other, and actual terminal correspondence remains pending.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and initial easterly interval north of Ingeniero Foster and La Maruja
correspondence.finding: The initial channel and first six part joins are not established by the regional lagoon map. No headwater name is supported.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward bend and northern easterly interval
correspondence.finding: The large regional label obscures part of this interval. Neither the northward link nor the adjoining eastward continuation is independently traced.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern middle turns and southward approach toward Caleufú
correspondence.finding: No inspected source traces the transfer across this sector or its intervening joins. A regional boundary cannot establish the modeled connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southward bend and easterly-to-northeasterly passage near Caleufú
correspondence.finding: Scattered mapped lagoons do not demonstrate the selected entries, passages, exits or continuity across the transition between regional settings.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeasterly approach south of the mapped Chadilauquen lake
correspondence.finding: Chadilauquen is separately mapped north of this approach. The selected lake connection and onward eastern transfer are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Final eastward turns and actual inland endpoint east of Chadilauquen
correspondence.finding: No mapped name or inspected detailed correspondence identifies the actual endpoint or its final approach. It is not established as Chadilauquen or as another named lagoon.
